title: External audit bridge: validated sink connectors and operator controls for private/VPC/on-prem forwarding
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: Customers running Private / VPC / on-prem Redwood deployments need reliable, auditable forwarding of platform audit logs into customer-managed storage (S3-compatible blobstores, Azure Blob, GCS, and private object stores). Existing options are ad-hoc and place operational burden on customers to validate delivery semantics, encryption handling (CMEK), and retention lifecycle. This ticket scopes a hardened 'audit bridge' flow that validates sink compatibility, enforces integrity metadata, supports customer-managed KMS handshakes, and exposes operator-level controls in Console for RBAC/SSO admin roles.
acceptance_criteria: Audit Bridge connector validator implemented: can run validation against S3, GCS, Azure, and one S3-compatible private blobstore using a minimal agent and return a deterministic compatibility report
Signed upload mode: bridge supports signed URL upload flow for air-gapped or constrained egress customers and logs proof-of-delivery with per-batch SHA256 digest metadata
CMEK handshake documented and implemented: connector supports customer-provided CMEK key identifiers and securely negotiates envelope keys for uploads, with audit events recording key IDs used
Operator controls in Console: Admins (RBAC v2 role 'audit-admin') can configure sink connectors, run validation, view last-validated timestamp, and rotate sink credentials via UI actions
Retry and dead-letter policy: failed deliveries are retried with exponential backoff; after configurable threshold log batches land in a customer-visible DLQ with clear remediation steps
Security review completed and threat model accepted by Security team
E2E integration test against a temporary S3-compatible test fixture included in CI and passing
design_notes: We will implement a connector validation step that performs a set of deterministic checks: list/create/delete object lifecycle, multipart upload footprint, metadata preservation, ACL behavior, and SSE/KMS compatibility. For private/on-prem stores that disallow direct server-initiated uploads, we add a signed upload mode where the bridge issues short-lived presigned PUT URLs that the customer's transfer agent uses. Integrity is enforced by adding a batch-level metadata object that contains SHA256 of uploaded objects and a signed manifest produced with the bridge's attest key. The CMEK handshake leverages envelope encryption: bridge generates ephemeral data key, encrypts it with customer KMS (using key ID provided by customer) and stores encrypted data key alongside object metadata. Admin controls integrate with RBAC v2; only 'audit-admin' and higher can create or rotate connectors. We intentionally avoid storing long-lived secret blobs in the control plane: credentials are stored encrypted in customer KMS or provided to a local on-prem agent. Rollout will start with read-only validation, then presigned uploads, then full push-mode with retries.
implementation_tasks: Spec: write connector validation spec (checks, timeouts, error codes)
Bridge component: add 'validation' API and deterministic report schema
Presigned flow: implement presign endpoint and short-lived token issuance for on-prem agent
CMEK: implement envelope key flow and metadata formatting consistent with object-store providers
Console UI: add Audit Sink config page with 'Validate connection' action and last-validated timestamp
RBAC: wire 'audit-admin' role to new console actions and audit events for sink lifecycle
CI: add e2e job that runs validation against a local MinIO fixture and records results
Docs: author runbook for customers and operator troubleshooting guide
Security review: engage Security team and patch threat-model findings
testing_plan: Unit tests for connector validator behaviors and error mapping
Integration tests: MinIO (S3-compatible), Google Cloud Storage emulator, Azure Storage emulator
Presigned upload test that simulates limited egress: agent fetches presigned URL and uploads payload; bridge verifies manifest
CMEK roundtrip test using mock KMS endpoints and asserting encrypted data key metadata
Chaos test: simulate intermittent 5xx from storage and verify backoff and DLQ behavior
Security fuzzing: inject malformed metadata and ensure bridge rejects with consistent audit event
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): expose validation-only mode to 5 private deployments and internal infra tenants
Phase 2: enable presigned upload mode for customers with restricted egress; require operator opt-in
Phase 3: enable push-mode delivery for elect customers with monitoring and increased logging
Phase 4: GA: enable in Console with migration docs and default retry thresholds
Rollback: UI toggle to disable connectors and switch to 'retain only' local archive while debugging
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboard: per-connector last-validated timestamp, recent DLQ entries, and average roundtrip latency
notes: Follow-up work: add SAML-scoped admin groups mapping to 'audit-admin' role (PM ticket to scope)
Consider extension for immutability proofs using object-store retention policies and signed manifests
Customer beta candidates: FinancialCorp, HealthAppX — both requested CMEK + DLQ integration
Design decision: use presigned uploads for air-gapped scenarios to avoid long-lived control-plane egress credentials
